items.title: The Khalsa was founded at Vaisakhi 1699
items.claim: What did Guru Gobind Singh establish in 1699?

options.text: A new Sikh state in northern India
The Khalsa (the 'pure') — a community of initiated Sikhs marked by the Five Ks (Kesh, Kara, Kanga, Kachera, Kirpan), open to all castes and gender
A revised version of the Guru Granth Sahib
A peace treaty with the Mughal Empire

items.reveal:
At Anandpur on Vaisakhi (April) 1699, Guru Gobind Singh called for volunteers willing to die for the faith. The Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) came forward, were initiated with amrit (sweetened water stirred with a double-edged sword), and were then themselves used to initiate Gobind Singh.

The Five Ks: Kesh (uncut hair, including the dastaar turban), Kara (steel bracelet), Kanga (wooden comb), Kachera (cotton undergarment), Kirpan (small sword).

The Khalsa took the surname Singh (lion) for men and Kaur (princess) for women — symbolically equalising caste and gender.
items.why: Sikh identity has visible bodily markers that emerged from a specific 1699 event with named participants. The Five Ks are not vague cultural symbols but coded responses to Mughal-era persecution and caste hierarchy.

items.title: Dharma is a central but multi-layered Hindu concept

options.text: A complex term combining duty, righteousness, cosmic order and the proper way of life — context-specific (sva-dharma, one's own duty), stage-of-life-specific (ashrama dharma), and universal (sanatana dharma)

items.reveal:
The root dhr- means 'to hold' or 'sustain'. Dharma includes the cosmic order (rita in Vedic terms), social duty (varna dharma — duties of one's caste), age-appropriate duty (ashrama dharma — student, householder, forest-dweller, renouncer), and universal moral law (sanatana dharma).

The Bhagavad Gita (around 2nd century BCE) is the most influential text on dharma. Arjuna's crisis on the battlefield turns on the conflict between his duty as warrior (his sva-dharma) and his reluctance to kill kinsmen.

Krishna teaches that performing one's dharma without attachment to results (karma yoga) is the path to liberation.
items.why: Dharma has no single English equivalent. Translating it as 'religion' or 'duty' alone misses the richness — it shapes how Hindus understand both individual choice and cosmic order.

items.title: Diwali has multiple regional meanings

options.text: A single event — Rama's return to Ayodhya

Multiple events depending on region: Rama's return to Ayodhya (north India), Krishna's defeat of Narakasura (south India), Lakshmi's emergence (west India); also marks new year for some Hindu, Jain and Sikh communities

items.reveal:
Diwali (Sanskrit dipavali, 'row of lamps') falls in October-November on the new moon of Kartika. The five-day festival includes Dhanteras (wealth), Naraka Chaturdashi (Krishna's victory), Diwali itself (Lakshmi puja, Rama's return), Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj (siblings).

For Jains, it marks Mahavira's attainment of moksha. For Sikhs, it commemorates Guru Hargobind's release from imprisonment in 1619 (Bandi Chhor Divas).

The festival has become a major UK public event — Leicester's Diwali celebrations are the largest outside India.
items.why: Pan-Hindu festivals can have different narratives in different regions. Treating Diwali as a single myth misses how diverse Hindu practice is and how it links to neighbouring traditions (Jain, Sikh) at the same calendrical moment.
